title: SLO-driven multi-region routing with capacity-aware pinning and blackout resilience
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement an SLO-driven multi-region routing policy that combines latency-based routing, geo pinning, and capacity-aware steering plus explicit blackout-resilience behaviors. Goal: ensure 99th-percentile end-to-end latency SLOs for tiered customers while preventing cascading failures during regional capacity loss. Deliverables: routing policy implementation, operator runbook, dashboarding (SLOs + capacity signals), and an automated canary for rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Routing policy supports: (a) soft geo-pinning with configurable grace windows, (b) capacity-aware steering using region capacity tokens, and (c) latency-weighted failover with hysteresis
SLOs defined: p50/p95/p99 latency and availability per region with automated error-budget-based drainage and shedding actions
Circuit breaker triggers: per-region token exhaustion + p99 latency > 2x SLO for 1 minute results in partial-ejection and progressive shedding policies
Automated blackout detection: regional heartbeat + capacity delta heuristic triggers emergency global failover with staged ramp to avoid thundering herd
Operator runbook published (Confluence) and on-call playbook validated in a dry-run (internal incident simulation)
End-to-end tests and a canary job validate fallback and soft-pin behavior under synthetic load (results posted to dashboard)
Metrics and dashboards: region capacity, shard free slots, request latencies by percentile, error budget burn, CB state, and route decisions are visible in Console

design_notes: Soft geo-pinning: prefer home region for up to 95% of requests unless capacity hint or latency SLOs indicate otherwise; implement as probabilistic delta to avoid strict stickiness
Capacity tokens: regions report free GPU slots and a computed spare-token budget; router prefers region with >=X spare tokens for low-latency paths
Latency-weighted failover: compute expected p99 delta if a request is hedged; if expected cost > budget, fallback to nearest compatible model variant

Circuit breaker policy: three-state (Closed, Tripped, Recovering) with exponential backoff and linear ramp on recover; tripping requires both token exhaustion and p99 violation to reduce false positives
Blackout detection: combine control-plane footprint (missing heartbeats) with sudden capacity delta >40% within 90s to flag as blackout mode
Shedding strategy: first shed non-critical routes (background embeddings, long-polling diagnostics), then degrade soft features (structured output >100 tokens), finally enforce strict token limits
